title: why to what
subtitle: when "why am i like this" goes in circles

steps.text: "why" questions feel like they'll help. often they go in circles.
"what happened?" and "what's one next step?" tend to move.
which sounds more like you when you're upset?

options.label: lots of "why"
options.reply: really common. "why" feels like digging for an answer.

options.label: more "what now"
options.reply: nice. that's the move we're practicing.

options.label: a mix
options.reply: makes sense. most of us switch back and forth.

lines: why do i always ruin everything?
what actually happened was i forgot her birthday. one small next step is texting her tonight.
steps.reply: the second one gives you something to do. that's the point.

steps.text: in early studies, practicing concrete "what" and "how" thinking helped people step out of rumination.

steps.prompt: think of something that's been on your mind. one small next step is…
ideas: writing down one thing for tomorrow.

steps.text: when "why" goes in circles, try: what happened, and what's one next step?
next time you catch a "why am i…", swap it for "what's one next step?"

grounding.idea: concrete thinking training reduced rumination in early studies
